description: Fetch the archived content of a URL at a specific Wayback Machine timestamp. Resolves to the nearest available capture when the exact timestamp has no snapshot. Returns the capture as text — an HTML page as readable plain text with its markup stripped, another text type (plain text, JSON, XML, JavaScript) as stored — and the replay URL of the capture Wayback served, for browser access. A capture of a PDF, image, or other non-text file fails as non_text_capture. Long text comes one page at a time: has_more and total_chars say what remains, and char_offset reads further — pass resolved_timestamp as timestamp so every page comes from the same capture. Use ia_find_snapshots first to discover valid timestamps for a URL.

char_offset.description: Character offset (UTF-16 code units) into the capture's text where this page starts. For the next page, pass the previous char_offset plus max_chars, with the previous resolved_timestamp as timestamp so the page comes from the same capture. An offset at or past total_chars returns empty text.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters this page holds. Defaults to the server-configured maximum (IA_MAX_SNAPSHOT_CHARS, typically 50 000); a larger value is served at that maximum, with a notice.

timestamp.description: Target Wayback timestamp: 1–14 digits — YYYYMMDDHHMMSS or a prefix of it — or an ISO 8601 date or UTC date-time such as "2020-01-01" or "2020-01-01T12:00:00Z". A full 14 digits, such as resolved_timestamp or a timestamp from ia_find_snapshots, reads that capture, or the one Wayback redirects it to; a shorter value names a period and resolves to the capture nearest its end ("2015" can resolve to one from early January 2016); blank reads the latest capture. Example: "20200101120000" for noon on January 1, 2020.

url.description: The URL whose archived content to retrieve.

name: ia_get_snapshot

char_offset.description: Character offset (UTF-16 code units) this page starts at.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_timestamp`: timestamp is not blank, 1–14 digits, or an ISO 8601 date or UTC date-time, or names a month, day, hour, minute, or second no Gregorian date and time has. `no_snapshot_available`: No capture exists near the requested timestamp for this URL, the capture there is an archived error page — the HTTP 4xx or 5xx the site itself returned when it was captured — or the Wayback Machine refused the replay request with an HTTP 4xx, as it does for a site excluded from the archive; or the closest-capture lookup answered HTTP 403, 410, or 451, the Wayback Machine declining to serve the URL at all. `non_text_capture`: The capture Wayback served is not text — a PDF, image, archive, or other non-text media type — so it holds no text to return. `content_fetch_failed`: The archived page could not be fetched — the Wayback Machine answered HTTP 5xx after retries or 429, did not answer within the request timeout, or could not be reached, or refused the unmodified (id_) form of a text capture it had replayed — or its nearest capture could not be looked up: the closest-capture lookup found no capture or answered HTTP 429, or 408, 425, or 5xx after retries, or an unreadable response, and its CDX fallback failed or had no time left within the lookup deadline (the request timeout plus 25 s); or the lookup refused the request with another 4xx, did not answer within the request timeout, or could not be reached. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

has_more.description: True when the capture's text continues past this page; the notice names the char_offset and timestamp that read the next one.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters this page could hold — the requested max_chars, or the server maximum when the request omitted it or asked for more.

notice.description: Set when the capture is longer than the 4 MiB read limit (the text comes from its first bytes only), when max_chars is above the server maximum, or when more text follows this page — naming the char_offset and timestamp that read the next one.

replay_url.description: Wayback Machine replay URL (https://web.archive.org) of the capture the text came from — where the fetch ended after any redirect Wayback issued to the capture it served.

resolved_status.description: HTTP status Wayback replayed the capture the text came from with — the same capture as resolved_timestamp and replay_url.

resolved_timestamp.description: Timestamp (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) of the capture the text came from, read from replay_url.

text.description: One page of the capture's text: up to max_chars characters from char_offset. An HTML page is reduced to readable plain text: scripts, styles, comments, and tags removed, character references decoded, whitespace collapsed. Another text type (plain text, JSON, XML, JavaScript) is the body as archived, line breaks and markup kept. Taken from at most the first 4 MiB of the capture; a notice says so when it is longer.

total_chars.description: Length of the capture's whole text in characters (UTF-16 code units), counted over the same first 4 MiB the text comes from.

title: Get Wayback Machine Snapshot Content
